title: Gap-junction-perturbed worms also acquire the brain shape of the species they resemble

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Gap-junction-perturbed worms also acquire the brain shape of the species they resemble

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: G. dorotocephala regenerates whose heads resemble another species after octanol treatment also have brain morphologies (length/width ratio, by anti-synapsin staining) resembling the brains of wild-type worms of that species.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 2. Results › 2.4. Brain Structure of GJ-Perturbed Worms Is Also Altered to That of Other Species

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Strikingly, we found that pseudo worms possessed brain morphologies that look like the brain morphologies of wild-type worms whose head shapes they resembled (Figure 4D–F) (ANOVA, p < 0.001).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M, Durant F, Hammelman J, Bessonov N, Volpert V, Morokuma J, Pinet K, Adams DS, Pietak A, Lobo D, Levin M, “Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms”, International journal of molecular sciences (2015), doi:10.3390/ijms161126065; section “2. Results › 2.4. Brain Structure of GJ-Perturbed Worms Is Also Altered to That of Other Species”. Scope: Octanol-treated G. dorotocephala regenerates compared with wild-type G. dorotocephala, D. japonica and S. mediterranea

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2015-girardia-04: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.69

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The outcome is a standard anatomical ratio with a clear comparison. Published measurements cover only selected species and do not provide a clearly complete raw dataset, allowing partial rather than definitive resolution.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Blindly measure brain length-to-width ratios in anti-synapsin images and compare pseudo worms with wild-type reference species. Concordance between external head class and the nearest reference brain distribution supports the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
P. felina was not adequately represented.

Raw microscopy images and per-worm values are not clearly deposited.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.95
analysis feasibility: 0.8
data adequacy: 0.5
discriminating power: 0.7
data existence: 0.55

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Brain aspect ratio is a standard morphometric variable, and the paper reports a significant group difference. The ratios and images needed to recompute it are not deposited, and no independent staining dataset repeats the octanol comparison. The result stays testable only with those measurements or a new assay.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure brain length-to-width ratio from synapsin-stained heads, blinded to external shape class, and test whether induced Girardia brains cluster with the reference species they resemble. A null or reversed clustering would refute the co-transformation.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
External head class and brain class were scored in the same animals, so the resemblance judgment can couple the two readouts.

Per-animal brain measurements are not in a public file.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

data existence: 0.32
analysis feasibility: 0.32
operationalizability: 0.78
discriminating power: 0.38
